title: The typed-position join withdraws Safe functions through AST closure classes that rules 5l and 5i read as unbound
why: Rule 10o serves, at every P2 statement and P3 position of a function the lexical reader reads, the join of the extended lexical closure and the rule-10l AST closure. After rule 10o the lexical closure reads every nested, for-clause, later-declarator, parenthesised and brace-initialiser assignment (the re-emitted disputed set, docs/reports/w47-lexical-closure-nested-assignment/artifacts/after/disputed-corpus.json, has no root of those classes left that the AST binds and the lexical closure does not), so what the join still adds are AST classes the lexical closure reads under established rules: a statement-expression value (rule 5l's container_of element: 127 admitted-row roots in 32 corpus function records, 498 in the system slice), a sub-object store whose root is the admitted store's own (rule 5i; including file-scope objects), and a static array initialiser counted by the AST's may_bind. Measured withdrawals (Safe -> Unknown, none an unsound Safe): corpus mk_fifo_queue_get (q), mk_plugin_cap (plugin), rd_kafka_Uuid_str (bytes), unit_test_telemetry_decoded_int64 (unit_test_data); system flb_engine_get_chunk_backpressure_percent (ins), sb_find_segregated_backlog_by_output_plugin_instance (backlog); plus summary cascades from the static inline flb_task_get_route_data/_status/set_route_status/set_route_data bodies. DISCHARGE: the AST closure reads rule 5l's admitted container_of element and rule 5i's admitted scalar or never-bound sub-object store as the lexical rules do (or the join is narrowed to the binding classes the lexical closure models, with a stated argument), with matching audited Lean, negative controls (a statement expression holding a custody call, a sub-object store of a tracked value) and a measured re-pin restoring the six without flipping any other row.

title: Token-adjacency write readers do not see a parenthesised destination `(x) = ...`
why: Rule 10o reads a parenthesised destination (the macro-expanded spelling: TAILQ_FOREACH's `(var) = ...`) in the never-bound closure, may_bind, O04-B08's store-base premises and the protected-formal alias closure. Other readers that find writes by token adjacency (`name =`) still do not: container_publication::CallerFormals::writes (rule 10d's unrebound formals), list_iteration::function_facts (rule 5l's element-only names and `written`), member_release's P1 and the return-family and sub-object-store readers. Measured by the rule-10o parity census over the pinned corpus: 803 parenthesised-destination records over the 17,850 function analyses (72 distinct spellings; tmp, _tmp, rkb, member, rkt ...), of which 0 are formals of their function (so rule 10d's stable formals are not affected at this pin); 0 in the Fluent Bit system slice. DISCHARGE: those readers take their writes from lexical_nested_assignment::written_names (a monotone refusal), with a measured re-pin.

title: The continued-access publication reader reads only a statement's first top-level store
why: publication.rs reads a continued-access store into a static destination (`G.f = p`, CTWIN-RESIDUALS) from a `;{}` run's first top-level simple `=`, the reading rule 10o replaced in the custody closure. The direction is fail-closed (a store it misses is not a publication, so nothing is discharged through it), so rule 10o registers it rather than widening it. Measured by the rule-10o parity census: 3,649 member-store records (summed over the 17,850 function analyses of the corpus) stand where that reader does not look (nested in a condition, a comma operand or a later position of their run; how many target a static destination is not measured), 0 in the system slice. DISCHARGE: the publication reader reads every member store through lexical_nested_assignment, refusing (not admitting) a nested one it cannot model, with a measured re-pin.
